run.exact_commands:
Driver script scratchpad/evalrun/gate1/run_one.sh, invoked once per (model,task):

cd scratchpad/study/src/harbor
uv run --no-dev harbor run --dataset "<dataset@version>" -i "<task>" --agent pi \
  --model "openrouter/<model-id>" --env docker -n 1 -q \
  --mounts '[{"type":"bind","source":"/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt","target":"/usr/local/share/ccr-ca-bundle.crt","read_only":true}]' \
  --ae OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-dummy \
  --ae "OPENROUTER_BASE_URL=http://172.17.0.1:18900/t/<tag>/api/v1" \
  --ae SSL_CERT_FILE=/usr/local/share/ccr-ca-bundle.crt --ae CURL_CA_BUNDLE=/usr/local/share/ccr-ca-bundle.crt \
  --ae NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/usr/local/share/ccr-ca-bundle.crt \
  --ve SSL_CERT_FILE=/usr/local/share/ccr-ca-bundle.crt --ve CURL_CA_BUNDLE=/usr/local/share/ccr-ca-bundle.crt \
  --ak max_turns=15 --ak model_api=openai-completions --ak version=0.87.1 \
  --jobs-dir <gate1/jobs/{sbv,tb2,dab}>

12 (dataset@version, task, model, tag) combinations:
spreadsheetbench-verified@1.0/10452 x {gemma-3-12b-it, gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, qwen3.5-9b}
terminal-bench-sample@2.0/regex-log x {gemma-3-12b-it, gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, qwen3.5-9b}
dabstep@1.0/dabstep-5 x {gemma-3-12b-it, gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, qwen3.5-9b}
dabstep@1.0/dabstep-70 x {gemma-3-12b-it, gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, qwen3.5-9b}
tags: gate1-<shortmodel>-<sbv|tb2>-<taskid> / gate1-<shortmodel>-dabstep-<5|70>

Full command list, task table, and per-run ledger numbers are in GATE1.md.
run.deviations:
Full detail in GATE1.md "Deviations" section. Summary:
1. CA-bundle mount (/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt) + SSL_CERT_FILE/CURL_CA_BUNDLE/NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS env vars on every run — this sandbox transparently TLS-intercepts all container egress; without trusting that CA, pi's install and HTTPS calls fail with self-signed-cert errors. Not needed on a real machine.
2. --ak model_api=openai-completions is mandatory (pi.py raises ValueError without it for custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints), not a style choice.
3. --ak version=0.87.1 pins pi explicitly (npm's current latest at run time) instead of leaving it to drift to whatever "latest" resolves to mid-run.
4. DABstep's two task Dockerfiles (dabstep-5, dabstep-70) were hand-patched in Harbor's local task cache (~/.cache/harbor/tasks/<hash>/<task>/environment/Dockerfile) to add a COPY of the CA bundle + PIP_CERT/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE/CURL_CA_BUNDLE/SSL_CERT_FILE env vars before the existing `pip3 install pandas` and `curl ...huggingface.co...` build steps, because pypi.org's HTTPS call failed the same self-signed-cert error at Docker build time (apt-get's plain-HTTP Ubuntu-mirror step needed no fix). Task content (instruction.md, test.sh, scorer.py, baked answers) was never touched. Each task was first run unpatched to confirm the failure was sandbox-network (reproducible, matches the SpreadsheetBench/Terminal-Bench deep-dives' identical finding), then retried once patched.
5. --ak max_turns=15 kept from the deep-dive recipe. Not an official default for any of the 3 benchmarks (DABstep baseline caps at 10 steps, SpreadsheetBench multi-round defaults to 5, Terminal-Bench has only a wall-clock cap) — it's pi's own turn-cap kwarg, needed because pi's own default is unbounded turns. 2 of the 12 runs (gemma-4-26b on tb2-regex-log and dabstep-70) hit this cap without finishing, confirming it was doing real, necessary work rather than an arbitrary restriction.
6. Official per-task timeouts (DABstep 1800s/600s, SpreadsheetBench 600s/600s, Terminal-Bench 900s/900s) were kept unmodified; no --timeout-multiplier used.
7. 3 infra re-runs per the "re-run once after fixing infra" rule: gemma-3-12b x SpreadsheetBench 10452 (Docker Hub 429 rate limit pulling python:3.11-slim — fixed by pre-pulling, retried), and gemma-3-12b x DABstep-5 / DABstep-70 (Dockerfile CA fix above, retried). Only the second (real-model) attempt of each is reported as the run's result; no model-level failure was ever retried.
run.images_kept: Kept (needed again for DABstep/SpreadsheetBench, both under budget): ghcr.io/laude-institute/t-bench/ubuntu-24-04:20250624 (183MB, DABstep's base image) and python:3.11-slim (189MB, SpreadsheetBench's base image). Total kept: 372MB, well under the 6GB allowance. Removed after use: ghcr.io/laude-institute/terminal-bench/regex-log:2.0 (118MB, Terminal-Bench's prebuilt image, not on the keep-list). All per-task Harbor environment containers/images were deleted automatically by Harbor's own --delete default after each trial — nothing task-specific was left behind. docker ps -a and docker images confirmed clean of anything beyond the two kept base images after cleanup. Disk headroom stayed at 13-15GB avail (df -h /) throughout, never approached the shared ~15GB limit. Docker daemon was never stopped; no images belonging to other agents were pruned (only a python:3.11-slim pull, a regex-log image we removed ourselves, and DABstep/SBV task-image builds that Harbor auto-deleted).

runs.notes: 1 LLM call, 2 trajectory steps. Wrote a coherent plan plus a fenced ```json array naming bash/write/read as plain assistant text instead of a real pi tool call. Zero tool calls executed; trial ended after turn 1. Same mechanical failure on all 4 of this model's tasks.

runs.task: dabstep-70 (DABstep, dev split, easy, manual-required trap question)
runs.notes: Same fake-JSON-tool-call pattern as dabstep-5; named the right file to open (fraud_monitoring_protocol.txt) but never actually invoked a tool. First attempt on this task (unpatched Dockerfile) hit an infra RuntimeError (pip SSL cert failure); re-run once after patching the cached Dockerfile with CA trust, per the retry-once rule.

Wrote correct-looking openpyxl Python plus a fake JSON tool-call array; never executed anything, output file never written. First attempt hit an infra failure (Docker Hub 429 pulling python:3.11-slim, shared rate limit); re-run once after pre-pulling the image.
Produced a plausible regex in prose/markdown but again as fake tool-call JSON, not a real pi tool invocation; /app/regex.txt never written.
Correct answer, 7 real tool calls, fast (57s).

runs.task: dabstep-70 (DABstep, dev split, easy, manual-required trap question)
runs.failure_mode: timeout while working / ran out of turns
runs.notes: Hit the --ak max_turns=15 cap with real tool calls throughout (cumulative prompt reached 538k tokens by turn 15); never converged on writing /app/answer.txt. Genuine capability limit, not an infra or format issue. This is the single most expensive run of the 12 ($0.038).
Correct answer after 10 real tool calls.

runs.failure_mode: timeout while working / ran out of turns
runs.notes: Hit the 15-turn cap with active tool use throughout; /app/regex.txt never written in time. Last trajectory step's message field is empty (mid-tool-call when the turn cap fired).

runs.task: dabstep-70 (DABstep, dev split, easy, manual-required trap question)
runs.notes: Correctly opened manual.md, correctly computed the 9.13% fraud rate from payments.csv, then misread manual.md's illustrative fee-band example (7.7%-8.3%) as a hard fine threshold and answered 'yes' where gold is 'Not Applicable' -- same failure shape independently reproduced in the earlier deep-dive's live smoke of this exact task under the baseline smolagents driver.

Correctly diagnosed the vertical-lookup logic and computed all 9 matching rows, but wrote only the first 5 of 9 into the required E4:E12 range -- an off-by-N truncation on an otherwise-correct solution.

runs.failure_mode: reasoning used up the output budget
runs.notes: Burned its entire 16,384-token completion/reasoning budget on a single call with no tool call and no visible text produced; /app/regex.txt never written. Reproduces the earlier deep-dive's identical finding on this exact task+model.
